answer: Resist sybils with a unique hardware root and a non-transferable, time-locked bond that matures only after a delayed peer review of boot measurements, key lineage, and work traces. Vouchers who admit the newcomer lock matching stake. Picture a survey crew planting timber across a glacier that feeds a canyon: what looks like many ledges is still one moving mass, and a later split is obvious once the flow is watched over time. If two accounts share a root, slash both bonds and the vouchers. Continuous uniqueness checks make a shell farm cost more than one honest agent.
